pattern: scripts/lib/module-graph.mjs (and everything built on it -- docs/MODULE-MAP.md, test/deadExports.test.ts's reachability gate) only sees static `import ... from "..."` clauses; a file reached only via a dynamic `await import(...)` reads as unreachable/demo-only/dead when it is actually live, so any dead-code or reachability finding from this tool can be silently wrong wherever a dynamic import exists.

A test file that computes or asserts something fallible at MODULE TOP LEVEL (outside any test() callback) -- reading a file whose existence it assumes, asserting a string exists in it -- throws during test/run.mjs's own `await import(outfile)` loop, which has no try/catch. The throw does not crash visibly: node:test's own runner absorbs it (visible only as an easy-to-miss "asynchronous activity after the test ended... caught by the test runner" diagnostic line), and test/run.mjs's loop silently stops counting every file imported after the crashing one in its final summary -- a plausible-looking, genuinely-smaller pass/fail total, not an error. Recurs whenever a test file's own setup code (not its test bodies) can throw on stale assumptions about a file's content.

scripts/_mutcheck.mjs accepts exactly one test file per invocation and scores EVERY mutation targeting the given source file against it -- so when two different test files each cover different properties of the SAME shared source file (e.g. public/scoring.js, tested by both test/scoring.test.ts and test/terrainContribution.test.ts), running _mutcheck.mjs against either one alone correctly reports the OTHER file's own mutations as SURVIVED (out of scope for that run), and scripts/mutate-results.mjs's own upsert-by-id design (FIX-6) then overwrites their previously-correct CAUGHT record with that scoped-wrong SURVIVED one. Recurs for any source file covered by more than one test file whenever _mutcheck.mjs is run against just one of them.
